title: The *Bill* Arrives
dek: Criminal probes, agentic privacy breaches, and the safety architect walking away: the costs of deploying agents without an authorization model.

stories.label: per million input tokens, undercutting rivals at frontier benchmarks
stories.headline: The midrange model tier is now where the benchmark war is being fought.
The consent architecture was never designed for agents that act across permission domains.
An AI coding agent committed a credential to GitHub. Four months of prompts exposed.

stories.short: Arizona goes criminal on AI agents
stories.headline: Criminal liability is a different conversation from safety benchmarks; the labs built one.

stories.short: NGA asks Congress for AI floor
stories.headline: States have legislated AI for 18 months. The NGA plan crystallizes what Congress can't nullify.

stories.label: Anthropic IPO price, above range, as its chief safety architect walked
stories.headline: The researcher who built the benchmarks says they're being used to certify the wrong things.

stories.short: South Korea: AI cheating at exam
stories.label: students in Korea's college exam amid AI cheating nobody planned for
stories.headline: Nobody has built credible AI detection for high-stakes testing. Both countries held the exam.

still_signal: Every agent story today is about a system that worked as designed. The problem isn't that they're unsafe. It's that 'safe' was never defined for agents.
